articles.title: Rohingya who escaped Myanmar’s genocide tell their stories
articles.description: Survivors recount rivers red with blood and burning nearby villages serving as an urgent warning to flee their homes Smoke was often the signal to run – seen from a distance, it was the indication for Rohingya that a neighbouring village was under attack and that theirs would be next. In other places, they saw the rivers run red and would pull out the bodies, perform quick burial rites and then flee.

articles.title: ‘A new record for entertainment’: Grand Theft Auto VI sales hit $3.8bn on first day of release, developer says
articles.description: The announcement from Rockstar Games would mean GTA VI has already earned more than the entire box office run of the highest-grossing film of all time Grand Theft Auto VI generated $3.79bn in retail sales on its first day , publisher Rockstar Games has announced, calling it the biggest launch for any entertainment product in history. The worldwide figure was based on company estimates through the end of the day Thursday, the day the game launched. Rockstar said also it had sold 32.5m units of the game on prerelease, setting a record across platforms.

articles.title: Man accused of sparking deadly Los Angeles wildfire found guilty
articles.description: Verdict in case against former Uber driver Jonathan Rinderknecht comes after first trial ended with hung jury The 30-year-old accused of sparking the deadly Palisades fire in Los Angeles was found guilty of two federal arson charges in a Friday verdict that came months after his first trial concluded with a hung jury. For two weeks, a fresh batch of jurors listened to prosecutors mount their case against Jonathan Rinderknecht.

articles.title: Victorian Greens seek urgent injunction over how-to-vote cards mimicking party’s branding but preferencing it last
articles.description: Exclusive: Independent candidate Tosh-Jake Finnigan’s cards instruct people to vote in a way that would benefit Liberal party Get our daily political email , free app or daily news podcast The Victorian Greens are seeking an urgent injunction from the supreme court to stop an independent candidate distributing how-to-vote cards that allegedly mimic the party’s branding and urge people to preference it last. As prepoll opened on Wednesday morning, Tosh-Jake Finnigan’s campaign team handed out how-to-vote cards that used the minor party’s colour scheme, font and triangle logo with the banner “Vote 1 Green Values”.

articles.title: Trump turns White House press conference into a 2028 succession audition
articles.description: The president appeared to put Vance and Rubio through their paces as potential successors, though Stephen Miller unexpectedly stole the spotlight “Which of you shall we say doth love us most?” The ageing King Lear’s question to his daughters, expecting them to compete for his favour and carve up his kingdom, hovered in the White House press briefing room on Friday.

articles.title: ‘A source of inspiration’: California celebrates the late civil rights icon Dolores Huerta
articles.description: A public vigil and celebration of life honor the civil rights activist and co-founder of United Farm Workers union Hundreds of people came out to honor and celebrate the life and legacy of the California civil rights activist Dolores Huerta at a celebration-of-life event Friday in Bakersfield. Huerta’s daughter Lori de Leon thanked attendees for their support during her mother’s passing, highlighting the widespread tributes and communities gathering in her honor.

articles.title: Republican senator blocks Trump cyber nominee over January 6 denial
articles.description: Thom Tillis move comes after Michael LoSapio, nominated for Cisa role, told hearing ‘I don’t believe it was an attack’ Senator Thom Tillis, the outgoing North Carolina Republican who is due to be replaced by a Democrat, has reportedly blocked a confirmation vote on Donald Trump’s nominee to lead a key US cybersecurity agency, Michael LoSapio, after he denied during a hearing that the Capitol was attacked on January 6 2021. Tillis, who declined to run for re-election and after repeated clashes with Trump’s, confirmed to HuffPost on Friday that he has placed a hold on LoSapio’s nomination to serve as a director of the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Agency (Cisa). His block on the nomination will prevent it from being included in a package of nominees to be voted on next month, before the Republicans lose their majority in the Senate.

articles.title: NSW passes Mount Pleasant coalmine law as Greens claim change an attempt to head off One Nation
articles.description: Labor says allowing mine to increase production reflects ‘gravity of situation facing hundreds of workers’ – but critics call it ‘unprecedented and dangerous’ After a marathon session in the legislative council on Friday, the Minns government and the Coalition voted at 1.36am on Saturday morning to allow the Mount Pleasant mine to increase its annual extraction rate from 12.5MT to 16.5MT until 2032.

articles.title: French police officers found guilty of racist assault on black music producer
articles.description: Beating of Michel Zecler in 2020 sparked outrage over police brutality after it was caught on security cameras Three French police officers who beat a black music producer they said was not wearing a face mask during the Covid pandemic have been found guilty of intentional, racist violence. The brutal assault on Michel Zecler, now 47, was caught on security cameras in his building in 2020 and triggered outrage in France over police brutality. The trial this month was considered a turning point for the recognition of racist violence.

articles.title: Trump says he discussed Jensen Huang with Xi; Bessent tells CNBC Nvidia chip export policy is unchanged
articles.description: Trump said he discussed Jensen Huang with China's Xi. Bessent said the ousted Nvidia CEO didn't come up in talks he had while in China.

articles.title: Trump threatens ‘tremendous penalties’ for US tech firms that build datacenters abroad
articles.description: President gives wide-ranging White House press conference and says he has ‘fantastic relationships’ with Putin and Xi Donald Trump threatened on Friday to impose “tremendous penalties” on American tech companies that build datacenters outside the US, though he gave no details and told reporters he had not yet informed his own officials about the plan. In a discursive press conference from the White House briefing room, Trump also said he would “look into” the report that Iran had been planning to possibly detonate a “dirty bomb” in Washington DC, and backed JD Vance over comments the vice-president made blaming Republican midterm losses on the Iran war.

articles.title: Nasdaq erases all 2026 gains as AI sell-off dampens Anthropic’s second day of trading
articles.description: The Nasdaq lost trillions in value, with the AI startup’s IPO failing to buoy it as investors question huge sums being poured into AI buildout Who are Anthropic’s seven co-founders, now worth $180bn? As Anthropic’s stock dropped during its second day of trading, the wider stock market dipped with it. On Friday, the Nasdaq Composite erased all its gains for 2026 and closed down 5% from its value on 1 January. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 closed in correction territory. Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO failed to stem a global sell-off in AI-linked companies, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq erased some $4tn in market value this week, according to the Wall Street Journal.

articles.title: JP Morgan boss says he will find ways to offset ‘unfair’ rise in UK tax on banks
articles.description: Jamie Dimon says he is ‘setting an example’ in seeking to claw back Labour’s increase in surcharge, from 3% to 6% Jamie Dimon, the chief executive of JP Morgan, has said he will find ways to offset the chancellor’s tax rise for banks, calling the increase unfair. Speaking at an event in London on Thursday, Dimon said he would seek to claw back the increase and was “setting an example so that [governments] understand the trade-offs of these unfair penalties”.

articles.title: Police arrest teacher who missed sentencing after indecent assault conviction
articles.description: Sally-Anne Bowen was found guilty of having sexual relationships with two pupils at a boys’ school in the 1980s A chemistry teacher who had sexual relationships with two pupils at a boys’ school in the late 1980s has been arrested by police in Hampshire after she failed to turn up to her sentencing hearing. Sally-Anne Bowen, 65, could not be found at her home by Metropolitan police officers on Friday morning after a warrant was issued for her arrest, a court heard.

articles.title: Florida mechanic found guilty of murdering British woman who attorney says came to US to die
articles.description: Dwain Hall was convicted of stabbing Sonia Exelby, a music teacher who prosecutors say suffered from mental illness A Florida mechanic has been found guilty of stabbing to death a British music teacher, whom he convinced to travel to the United States. Dwain Hall, an auto repair and tow truck driver, groomed 32-year-old Sonia Exelby from Portsmouth, England, on a fetish website before luring her to the US.

articles.title: Spain frees wealthy US-sought activist on bail as Irish police raid Dublin home
articles.description: Pro-Palestinian donor James ‘Fergie’ Chambers released as court considers extradition request In a blur of events surrounding the Trump administration’s effort to extradite James “Fergie” Chambers, Spain released the wealthy US activist and donor on bail even as Irish police raided a Dublin house owned by Chambers and his partner, Stella Schnabel, acting on a request from US authorities. Chambers’s case is the first known instance of the US seeking to extradite a citizen over alleged support for Hamas, an accusation apparently tied to an international money-laundering charge in the criminal complaint underpinning the extradition request and donations to organizations helping Palestinians in Gaza.

articles.title: Indian man sentenced to 19 years in prison for conspiring to kill Sikh separatist in New York
articles.description: Nikhil Gupta admitted to plotting with Indian government official to hire hitman to murder dual US-Canadian citizen An Indian ⁠man was sentenced to more ⁠than 19 ​years in US prison on Friday after admitting to orchestrating a failed Indian government-backed plot to kill a Sikh separatist in New York ⁠City , in connection with what US and Canadian authorities have called a broader effort to target Indian dissidents. Nikhil Gupta, 55, pleaded guilty in February to murder-for-hire, conspiracy ⁠to commit murder-for-hire and conspiracy to commit money laundering.

articles.title: Misty-eyed Burnham gambles on closer ties with EU as he throws down gauntlet to Tories and Reform
articles.description: PM challenges rivals to rebuff plan he says could add 0.5% annual growth to economy and offer young people hope Several sentences into a slightly convoluted answer about where UK-EU relations might go next, Andy Burnham abruptly changed tack. “The important point is that the Britain of today and the EU of today is not the one of 2016,” he said. “Life has moved on in so many ways.” This is undoubtedly true. But Burnham’s political gamble on closer ties with Brussels hinges on the assumption that most British voters feel this way as well.

articles.title: Two men killed after glider crashes into Loch Leven in Scotland
articles.description: The pair had taken off from the Scottish Gliding Centre at nearby Portmoak on a training flight Two men have been killed after their glider crashed into Loch Leven, a large body of water in Perth and Kinross, on Friday morning. Police Scotland said their bodies were recovered from the loch by the emergency services after the alarm was raised at 11.05am on Friday.

articles.title: Denmark to expel Russian diplomat over alleged Moscow link to attempted killing of rapper
articles.description: Russian intelligence thought to be behind plan to kill US-Ukrainian musician Kyivstoner before concert in Denmark Denmark’s foreign minister has said Russia’s defence attache in Copenhagen would be expelled after Moscow was suspected of being behind an attempted killing of a US-Ukrainian rapper. “We have just summoned the Russian ambassador to the ministry of foreign affairs and notified him of the government’s decision to expel the Russian defence attache from Denmark,”, Lars Løkke Rasmussen told a news conference. The expulsion will happen within seven days.

articles.title: No one else in Reform is suitable to lead the party, Nigel Farage says
articles.description: Farage issues warning to potential rivals and says he will fight next election as leader if ‘still here and fit and healthy’ Nigel Farage has said he does not see another person who could do his job as leader of Reform UK, in a warning shot to potential rivals who might seek to replace him. The Reform UK leader delivered a message that he was going nowhere despite his worries over his personal safety in the wake of the killing of the Reform politician Ann Widdecombe.

articles.title: Bitcoin's regulation bull case is played out. What could drive crypto gains moving forward
articles.description: Crypto investors are looking beyond Congress for the next catalyst after the Senate failed to advance the Clarity Act in September.

articles.title: EU wants ‘closest possible relationship’ with UK after agreeing Brexit reset deal – live
articles.description: President of European Council says EU ‘remains open to have the closest possible relationship’ with the UK Senior correspondent Making today’s reset deal contingent on a further agreement on the level of tuition fees for EU citizens is designed to neutralise the leverage London gets in the next six months, EU sources have said. Senior diplomats had already confirmed this week that the EU would defer the deal on the level of tuition fees for another six months , a move designed to give the UK leverage in parallel negotiations to have the UK included in Made in Europe legislation designed to protect EU supply chains against China. But the move to make the food and drink deal also contingent on a tuition fees deal effectively seeks to neutralise the leverage the UK gets today. This is a serious chess game and shows the EU, again, is willing to speak very warmly about the UK but will play absolute hard ball when it comes to conceding any points to a former member state. It was the same point France was making last night insisting the UK could not have voting rights on legislation in relation to food and drink. During his meeting with businesses in Brussels, PM Burnham said his EU deal would add up to 0.5% to the UK’s GDP. “We’re pretty much there, and it’s a really good deal.” “Treasury analysis out today is saying that now it’s clear up to 0.5% on GDP as a result of the deal. The single biggest growth intervention in this Parliament.”

articles.title: US reacts cautiously to Myanmar genocide ruling as EU praises ‘critical’ role of UN’s top court
articles.description: Reactions to ICJ ruling underline global divisions over court with China raising concerns about judicial overreach The US has greeted with caution the world’s highest court’s ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, while China has raised concerns of judicial overreach. Reactions to Thursday’s historic ruling underlined deep international division over the role of the court and similar institutions. The international court of justice (ICJ) had never previously found a state responsible for genocide and the decision could set a precedent for future genocide claims, notably a case against Israel .

articles.title: ‘Weak and dizzy’: the secretive ICE force-feeding tactics that ended a Cuban father’s hunger strike
articles.description: Exclusive: Luis Alejandro Cora Pérez says in messages to Guardian from inside Texas facility pain of force-feeding caused him to break strike The text message that came from inside the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention center was stark: “I have spent five days eating regular food. If I don’t eat it, they put the tube in me to feed me.” A Cuban asylum seeker, Luis Alejandro Cora Pérez, 32, said in messages to the Guardian this month that he was still weak and dizzy after three months without eating, but that he had broken his hunger strike because being force-fed was just too painful.

articles.description: State attorney says scandal ‘raises bright red flags’ and aims to find out if company misled investors California has served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia after a scandal that prompted the departure of co-founder and longtime chief executive Jensen Huang. Rob Bonta, the US state’s attorney general, issued the subpoena as part of an investigation into whether exports of the California-based company’s advanced semiconductor chips ended up in China, contravening US restrictions.

articles.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
articles.description: Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years. Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.

articles.title: Race to be next UN secretary general exposes divisions among world powers
articles.description: Debate about dominance of permanent five members could reignite if major powers block Costa Rican frontrunner The race to become the next UN secretary general could reach a decisive moment on Friday when a UN security council vote is likely to reveal whether the Costa Rican frontrunner for the post would be blocked by the big powers. If so, the setback will reignite a debate about the dominance of the permanent five (P5) members at the United Nations. Rebeca Grynspan, an economist and UN insider who is from a family of Polish-Jewish wartime refugees to Costa Rica, has been in the lead in all but one of the eight straw polls of the 15 UN security council members since the first secret ballot was held on 30 July. Each member goes down the list of candidates, casting an “encourage”, “discourage” or “no opinion” vote for each candidate.

articles.title: Iraq university’s removal of male professors teaching women sparks weeks of protests
articles.description: Al-Qadisiyah University’s move a sign of the country’s slide into a Taliban-like gender segregation, say activists The removal of male professors teaching female students at a university in southern Iraq has sparked protests and been criticised by activists as a Taliban-like gender segregation policy. As many as 400 women are estimated to have joined protests over the past two weeks calling for the return of their professors at Al-Qadisiyah University in a move that appears to have surprised its administrators.

articles.title: Myanmar ruling gives new relevance to genocide convention and is ‘full of messages’ for Israel
articles.description: Hailed as ‘a rare moment of justice’, judges’ decision sets out a roadmap for assessing the question of intent The international court of justice (ICJ) verdict making Myanmar the first country in history to be found guilty of committing genocide does not just deliver justice for Rohingya victims. It also gives the 1948 genocide convention new relevance in governing the actions of nation states. In their nine votes to six majority ruling, the panel of judges in The Hague set out a detailed roadmap for how the convention should be applied to real-world situations in which a government is accused of committing genocide against a whole population group, especially when it comes to assessing the question of intent.

articles.title: China, Russia and US agree peace declaration with no mention of Ukraine and Iran wars
articles.description: Xi, Putin and Trump outline priorities that include UN reform, boosting oil supplies and ‘protection of diplomatic immunity’ China, Russia and the US say they have agreed a peace statement after an unprecedented trilateral summit, but the declaration made no mention of the wars in Ukraine and Iran caused by two of the participants. The declaration on Thursday also outlined a set of priorities that included changing the UN, boosting oil supplies and what it said was the protection of diplomatic immunity.

articles.title: Trump accused of falling asleep during Xi Jinping speech at Apec summit in China
articles.description: US president appeared to doze off while Chinese leader made speech, but White House insisted he was awake Donald Trump was, again, accused of falling asleep during a televised event, this time during the speech of the Chinese president, Xi Jinping, at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit in China. The US president appeared to close his eyes for roughly 10 seconds on Thursday. As his eyes closed, Trump’s head tilted downward, and his hands remained clasped in front of him.

articles.title: ‘Everyone struggled for this justice’: tears in court as Rohingya vindicated in Myanmar genocide ruling
articles.description: Relief in the immediate aftermath of a landmark ruling, but what happens next is in the hands of governments around the world There were tears in the halls of The Hague in the Netherlands and an eruption of applause in the refugee camps of Bangladesh as the scattered communities of Rohingya watched the UN’s top court rule the Myanmar military had committed genocide against them. For almost a decade, the Rohingya have awaited this moment; recognition from the international court of justice (ICJ) that Myanmar in 2017 intentionally tried to destroy the mostly Muslim minority group through a campaign of mass killings and rape. More than 10,000 Rohingya were killed and 700,000 fled to neighbouring Bangladesh.

articles.title: Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya minority, world’s top court rules
articles.description: Judgment finds ‘intent to destroy a substantial part of the Rohingya population’ after case seen as critical test for dealing with most serious of state crimes Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority during a 2017 military campaign, the world’s highest court has ruled, in a historic and unprecedented decision. The judgment from the international court of justice (ICJ) – which has never previously found a state responsible for genocide – ends a seven-year legal battle that was seen as a critical global test for dealing with the most serious of all state crimes.

articles.title: 假裝在新西蘭、提前請假、搶購主機：粉絲為《GTA 6》做足準備

articles.title: Israeli tanks cross ‘yellow line’ boundary into Hamas-controlled central Gaza
articles.description: First incursion across boundary since ceasefire deal comes as Eisenkot seeks to form government without Netanyahu The Israeli military crossed into Hamas-controlled central Gaza on Wednesday in its first ground operation across the “yellow line” boundary since a fragile ceasefire was agreed last October, forcing dozens of displaced Palestinians to flee their tents. Israeli tanks rolled along the Salah al-Din road , Gaza’s main north-south route, a day after the US-backed Board of Peace, a body overseeing the ceasefire, accused Israel and Hamas of failing to honour their commitments to end hostilities.

articles.title: Eight injured after driver in Israel repeatedly rams car into Palestinians
articles.description: Arab MPs accuse politicians of fuelling hostility as footage shows driver accelerating towards Palestinians at four locations in Kafr Qasim Eight people were injured on Wednesday evening when a driver struck Palestinian residents at four separate locations in Kafr Qasim, a city in central Israel. Footage shared on social media appears to show the car accelerating towards people, all Palestinians, at several locations in the city, striking them before driving away. Three of those injured were in moderate condition, and several of the victims were women leaving a nearby wedding, the Times of Israel reported .

articles.title: 中美俄元首峰會：從烏克蘭、伊朗、和平宣言到承諾核對話
articles.description: 會後發表的中俄美元首和平宣言顯示，三國領導人承諾就「減少核風險、防止核擴散」展開對話，並就聯合國改革、能源穩定和國際刑事法院管轄權等議題達成四點共識。

articles.title: Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked
articles.description: The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia. The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions.

articles.title: APEC final day in photos: Trump, Xi and Putin shake hands; Takaichi kept at a distance
articles.description: Leaders gathered Thursday for the second day of the economic summit, ahead of a historic trilateral meeting between the U.S., Russia and China.

articles.title: 從領導人合照到場邊會談：高市早苗的APEC外交觀察
articles.description: 高市早苗在歡迎晚宴前與中國國家主席習近平握手，兩人短暫互動。不過，高市抵達深圳時的接待安排相對低調。

articles.title: AI是做精神導師，發佈教法裁決？穆斯林對此意見不一
articles.description: 穆斯林社群因伊斯蘭AI助手Qaf能否頒布教法裁決爆發爭議。開發者強調僅供學習，學者則警告不可取代專業裁決，反映AI與傳統宗教的張力。

articles.title: APEC的特色服飾：從克林頓皮衣到深圳「鯤鵬展翅」絲巾
articles.description: 在每一年的亞太經合組織峰會上，人們除了關心哪個國的領導人出席、他們之間的互動和談話，還有他們大合照時穿了什麼。

articles.title: Anthropic上市：七位即將成為億萬富翁的創辦人
articles.description: 開發AI聊天機器人Claude的Anthropic在美國上市，這將使其創辦人身價暴增。

articles.title: One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN
articles.description: Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report. In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund ( UNFPA ) published on Thursday.

articles.title: 中美俄「三巨頭」坐在了一起，世界正滑向大國共管嗎？
articles.description: 「他們能坐下來，就說明這個世界還沒有到第一次或第二次世界大戰那個狀況。」香港科技大學榮休教授丁學良對BBC說。

articles.title: Florida pastor found guilty over 2021 assassination of Haitian president
articles.description: Christian Emmanuel Sanon faces life in prison after conviction on charges arising from killing of Jovenel Moïse A Florida pastor with dual Haitian-American citizenship was convicted on Wednesday of US charges arising from the 2021 assassination of the Haitian president Jovenel Moïse. Christian Emmanuel Sanon was found guilty on charges including conspiring to kill Moïse after a nearly eight-week trial in federal court in Miami. He had faced a total of eight charges including conspiracy to kidnap or kill a person outside the United States.

articles.title: Hegseth uses Venezuela visit to boast of Maduro’s capture by US military
articles.description: Defense secretary asserts US dominance on trip that would have seemed ‘impossible, almost unbelievable’ a year ago Pete Hegseth has used his first visit to Venezuela since US special forces abducted its former president, Nicolás Maduro, to boast of the dictator’s capture during what he called “the single most sophisticated military operation in the history of Latin America”. Maduro was controversially seized by Delta Force operatives in the early hours of 3 January, setting in motion an improbable rapprochement between Washington and Venezuela’s anti-imperialist “Chavista” regime, which has ruled since 1999.

articles.title: Israel delays building contracts for West Bank settlement after UK sanctions
articles.description: Attorney general says E1 settlement decision should not be taken by caretaker government led by Netanyahu Israel has postponed issuing contracts for the construction of a large settlement on the West Bank seen as likely to render a two-state solution unviable, days after the UK imposed sanctions against building firms operating in the area. Israeli diplomats insisted the move was not in response to the measures from Downing Street . Gali Baharav-Miara, the attorney general, said any decision on settlement expansion should not be taken by the caretaker government led by Benjamin Netanyahu but by whatever new administration was formed.

articles.title: APEC深圳峰會：習近平親迎特朗普，46年來首次中國元首接機
articles.description: 這是中國自1980年以來，首次有最高領導人親赴機場迎接外國元首。1980年前，華國鋒、毛澤東都有多次赴機場迎接外國領袖的歷史。

articles.title: 黃仁勳掀「中國間諜」迷因：幽默與偏見之間，亞裔女性如何自處？
articles.description: 黃仁勳醜聞曝光後，網上湧現大量「中國間諜」、「美人計」笑話。這些看似無傷大雅的時事迷因，卻讓部分亞裔女性感到困擾。

articles.title: Fears grow that US will put Nobel-winning judge under sanctions after Myanmar genocide ruling
articles.description: A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay , if the court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide against the Rohingya. The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.

articles.title: Putin says EU is losing industry, falling behind competition, ahead of meeting with Trump and Xi
articles.description: Putin used the speech to emphasize Russia's economic resilience despite U.S. sanctions, and played up opportunities for APEC members in the country.

articles.title: European Commission accused of sugarcoating figures to release funds to Egypt
articles.description: Leaked documents raise questions about claims Egypt met welfare targets to qualify for €2.5bn in loans The European Commission has been accused of sugarcoating figures to enable it to release funds to Egypt under a landmark pact with the authoritarian government of Abdel Fatah al-Sisi. The charge relates to a €7.4bn deal promised by Ursula von der Leyen , the European Commission president, to al-Sisi on a high-profile visit to Cairo in 2024. The three-year “strategic and comprehensive partnership” was intended to bolster Egypt’s shaky economy, deter migrants from coming to Europe and shore up a region reeling from the 7 October attacks and Israel’s war on Gaza.

articles.title: 身體最常受傷、卻很少人會刻意鍛鍊的部位：腳踝
articles.description: 運動物理治療師珍妮薇芙·陶亞（Genevieve Tawiah）分享了她護理關節的秘訣；關節問題佔急診就診量的 5%。

articles.title: Caribbean nations fear economic impact of shuttering citizenship program after EU threats
articles.description: St Kitts and Nevis to wind down citizenship-by-investment program after EU warns of end to visa-free access The decision by St Kitts and Nevis to end a lucrative programme offering citizenship to wealthy foreigners in exchange for investment threatens its economy and ability to support people in need, the premier of the island of Nevis has warned. On Friday, Terrance Drew, the prime minister of the twin-island Caribbean nation, announced he would wind down the citizenship-by-investment (CBI) programme, after the European Union threatened to end visa-free access for St Kitts and Nevis.

articles.title: 高雄選戰「知識藍」對決「新潮流」，國民黨能複製「韓流」嗎？
articles.description: 柯志恩以「知識藍」的姿態拉攏中間選民，支持度大幅追貼深耕高雄20年的賴瑞隆，選情咬緊。

articles.title: 「藍白合」示範區：新竹市選情如何透露台灣第三勢力的未來？
articles.description: 新竹市是民眾黨此前唯一贏得執政權的縣市，現任市長高虹安尋求連任，她這次雖已退出民眾黨、改以無黨籍身分參選，但學者指出其選情不僅將影響雙方未來合作模式能否延續，也可能牽動2028年全國大選的政治布局。

articles.title: 「讓黃仁勳回歸」運動：輝達駁斥、特朗普支持恢復其CEO職位
articles.description: 多位科技業領袖表態支持一項行動，要求這家AI晶片龍頭讓黃仁勳重返執行長職位。

articles.title: 羅伯·派汀森：《暮光之城》男主角如何成為007
articles.description: 羅伯·派汀森（Robert Pattinson）早已在《暮光之城》系列、《蝙蝠俠》和《奧德賽》等電影，奠定了自己作為男主角、動作明星及演員的地位。如今，他接下詹姆士·龐德（James Bond；占士邦）一角，將使他的知名度更上一層樓。

articles.title: APEC深圳觀察：習近平想告訴世界，中國掌握著未來
articles.description: 當世界領導人本週齊聚深圳，他們將看到一座代表中國未來的科技之城：機器人、AI、摩天大樓，處處展現蓬勃的創新活力。但這很可能只是故事的一半：因為峰會停工的建築工人、為生計奔波的零工群體，對未來有著不同的想像。

articles.title: 里長赴中旅遊：台灣《反滲透法》為何「查辦多、定罪少」？
articles.description: 台灣「九合一」地方選舉進入倒數，北京試圖介入台灣選舉的相關活動再受關注。台灣《反滲透法》施行後，儘管近年相關案件數量快速增加，但查辦近600人，只有5人被定罪，使現行法律規範與執法標準受到外界檢視。

articles.title: 里長赴中旅遊受關注：為何北京鎖定里長？里長怎麼看？
articles.description: 台灣地方選舉即將到來，近年北京對台統戰工作重心從政商菁英轉向基層社會，而里長作為選舉期間的地方「樁腳」，就成為了北京的重要接觸對象。

articles.title: 無法複製的奇蹟？深圳如何從改革開放樣板到「中國矽谷」
articles.description: 深圳首次主辦亞太經濟合作組織（APEC）領導人峰會，成為中國的第三座主辦城市。深圳的崛起往往被視為中國改革開放最成功的一場實驗。而在中國和世界變幻莫測的今天，這個高速發展的奇蹟還能延續嗎？

articles.title: 九合一前夕：台灣幾乎年年選舉，會引起「投票疲勞」嗎？
articles.description: 台灣在過去七年間，幾乎每年都有大型選舉、罷免或公投。有學者形容台灣政治人物常處於「選舉模式」，在面對不同議題時往往急於回應。

articles.title: 「台灣乾爹」光環崩塌：黃仁勳事件如何震動產業、政治與社會？
articles.description: 黃仁勳光速跌落神壇的事件，讓台灣社會對他的崇拜、政治對他的政績綁定，以及產業對他個人的依賴重新校準。

articles.title: BBC調查揭英國「全球人才簽證」造假產業：中介助移民冒充藝術家及科技專才

articles.title: 從科技巨星到跌落神壇——黃仁勳如何深陷醜聞漩渦？
articles.description: 短短幾天內，黃仁勳作為全球科技競賽領軍人物、看似無可撼動的地位便迅速崩塌。

articles.title: 「你甚至不會告訴密友」：分娩後遺症，為何多年後仍揮之不去？
articles.description: 從失禁到長期疼痛，數以百萬計的女性在分娩數十年後仍然飽受後遺症困擾。

articles.description: 分析指排放或已提前達峰，但新煤電機組仍大量上馬，拐點成色有待檢驗。

articles.description: 簡和埃爾斯在幸福地生活了50年後，選擇接受安樂死，留下了他們唯一的孩子。

articles.title: 「短睡眠基因」：為何有人只需睡四小時？
articles.description: 一般成年人平均需要七至九小時睡眠，但有些人確實只需極少睡眠也能維持良好狀態。

articles.title: 從蔡康永、《VIVANT》到姆巴佩，北京為何區別處理「辱華」？
articles.description: 最近幾週，中國輿論場接連出現多宗被貼上「辱華」標籤的爭議事件：台灣藝人蔡康永、日本電視劇《VIVANT》以及法國球星姆巴佩。三宗事件看似性質相近，但官方反應與輿論熱度卻明顯不同，多位分析人士對BBC中文指出：這些差異背後是當局對於每個事件的定性並不相同。

articles.title: 「九合一」五大看點：「洋流」能否撼動台北？誰在卡位2028？
articles.description: 中共是否介入台灣選舉？ 這次選舉將如何影響賴清德與國民黨主席鄭麗文的政治能量？捲土重來、希望藉著地方議員選舉有所斬獲的小黨，此次結盟能否在主流政黨夾殺中突圍而出？

articles.title: DeepSeek被美國政府系統禁用：中美AI競爭繼續升溫
articles.description: DeepSeek的免費聊天機器人應用程式在Apple App Store下載排行榜上名列前茅，其AI模型也被美國科技企業採用。Snowflake、Vercel及OpenRouter等公司都已將DeepSeek整合至其提供給客戶的服務中。
